# From new information to an existing spec

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

A `State:` line is not part of that quote.

`$crav1-tighten-spec` stays for mushy wording.

A not-started spec (match status `not in the code`, or a thin spec) can keep taking information until planning. Adding information does not start planning and does not write `plan.md` or `tasks.md`. that is `python` on Windows and `python3` elsewhere, with `PYTHONUTF8=1` and `-X utf8`, including the notes index and `merge_safe_migrate.py`.

every input is saved once as one full note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` (by source date, with the import date recorded); for a fact, the fact plus the passage around it. The spec gets only its own short point with `Full source: <note>`, and the note gets the slug in `used_by`. Notes are never absorbed. The same source again is not imported twice; a disagreement is flagged as a conflict, never overwritten.

## First prompt

```text
$crav1-add-to-spec
@docs/specs/<slug>/

<the new information, in your words>

Add this to that spec. Do not write code. Do not plan.
```

To find code that no spec covers yet, with no change to point at, `$crav1-add-to-spec` is not the skill: run `$crav1-existing-to-specs recheck`, then bring a gap back here after a yes.

## Steps

| Phase | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Target | Named one `docs/specs/<slug>/`, or pick from the options | Options only when the target was not named, or more than one existing spec could fit. One option per spec folder. Does not ask for a typed slug. Does not create a slug |
| Add | — | Quotes the new information in that `spec.md`. Labels what is new versus what was already there. Inferred stays inferred. Does not invent acceptance, architecture, or tasks |
| Impact | If other files are affected, pick apply or leave them alone | Reads `docs/system/` and the other specs. Lists each proposed edit in one line. Does not edit those files until apply |
| Stop | Glance, then `$crav1-finalize-commit` if a changed file should be in git | Does not plan, implement, or commit |

No spec folders under `docs/specs/` (other than `_template`): the command stops and points at spark, ideas, intake, or match.

## What gets written

The target `docs/specs/<slug>/spec.md`, unless the new words were already there.

A mail, a transcript, a chat, a screenshot, or another original that is quoted is also written under `docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/`, with a `README.md`. The spec `Source:` and `Trace:` lines link to that folder.

`docs/system/` and other specs change only when apply is picked.

No `plan.md`. No `tasks.md`. A missing `docs/system/` is not seeded here. This command does not create `glossary.md`. A meaning the new information does not state is `to be researched`. A quote that is a yes for an `## Approval needed` item is not written as `Answered:` or `Approved:`.

On yes each note gains `Superseded <date> by <decision>.` A verbatim quote is left as it is.

## After

```text
Run next:
The new information is not tightened yet.

Tighten the spec:
`$crav1-tighten-spec orders-api`

Uncommitted: 1 file; commit with `$crav1-finalize-commit` when ready.
```

`scripts/ending.py --vendor codex` prints that block from the shared helper. When a `design/<topic>` branch is checked out or owns the change, the same helper shows a stay card first.

`$crav1-tighten-spec` names them when they apply, as the [New information on an existing slice](reference/workflow.md#new-info) route says. `$crav1-help next` gives the full order.

A handoff from `$crav1-read-environment` or `$crav1-suggest-tests-for-code` asks once at the end of that run, not once per item: The system picture may now be out of date. Run `$crav1-refresh-system-notes`?

A dump or a code change confirms the sort on one card: `yes (Recommended)`, or typed changes on that card's free-text answer. It does not say `table above` unless that table is in the reply.
